batchName: Roman Religion and Mythology (753 BC-AD 391) - Medium Batch 1

questions.question: Constantine's nephew became emperor in 361 and tried to revive the old cults. Where did he die two years later?
questions.explanation: His death in Persia ended the attempted pagan revival. In 380, under Theodosius, Christianity became the official religion.
questions.sourceQuote: His nephew Julian, emperor from 361, tried to revive the old cults, but died in Persia two years later.

questions.question: Roman tombstones were commonly dedicated *Dis Manibus*. What does that mean?
options: To the gods of the hearth
questions.explanation: Romans believed the dead joined the spirits of the underworld. Wealthier families sacrificed a sow at the funeral pyre.
questions.sourceQuote: Afterwards the dead were believed to join the spirits of the underworld, and tombstones were commonly dedicated "to the spirit-gods" (*Dis Manibus*).

questions.question: A Roman magistrate once forgot to mention "the Roman people" in a festival prayer. What happened as a result?
options: A second priest finished the prayer
The festival was cancelled for a year
The magistrate was stripped of office
The magistrate paid for an extra sacrifice
The entire festival started again from the beginning
questions.explanation: Prayers had to be word-perfect, and a single slip could spoil a ritual. So the whole festival had to be repeated from the start.
questions.sourceQuote: The entire festival had to start again from the beginning.

questions.question: Which statements describe Roman priesthoods? (select all that apply)
options: Priests formed a separate hereditary class
They were held by the same aristocrats who held political office
questions.explanation: Rome had no separate priestly class: politicians served as priests, married and led busy public lives. A priesthood was often sought as an honourable retirement.
questions.sourceQuote: Priesthoods were unpaid and held for life, and were often sought as an honourable retirement after a career in war and politics.

questions.question: What sign after Julius Caesar's death was taken as proof that he had joined the gods?
options: An eagle rising from his pyre
questions.explanation: A comet appeared during games held after his murder. Caesar had become chief priest in 63 BC, a sign of his rise.
questions.sourceQuote: A comet seen during games after his death was taken as proof that he had joined the gods.

questions.question: What was the mola salsa prepared by the Vestals?
options: A honey cake offered to the Lares
Grain left at tombs for the dead
Salted flour sprinkled on animals before sacrifice
questions.explanation: Because the mola salsa was sprinkled on every sacrificial animal, the Vestals' work touched every official sacrifice.
questions.sourceQuote: They prepared the *mola salsa*, a salted flour sprinkled on each animal before it was killed, and took part in festivals honouring the dead and the harvest.

questions.question: Which practices did Romans condemn as superstition (superstitio)? (select all that apply)
options: Exact public prayers by a priest
Vows made for victory in war
questions.explanation: Too much zeal was as dangerous as neglect. Grovelling, excessive devotion and prying into divine knowledge could anger the gods.
questions.sourceQuote: Fearful grovelling, excessive devotion and prying into divine knowledge were condemned as superstition (*superstitio*). Secret rites were suspect too, as possible magic or conspiracy.

questions.question: Once chosen, to whom did a Vestal Virgin answer?
questions.explanation: A Vestal was freed from her father's authority and, unusually for a Roman woman, needed no male guardian. She answered only to the chief priest.
questions.sourceQuote: She was freed from her father's authority and, unlike other Roman women, needed no male guardian, answering only to the chief priest.

questions.question: According to legend, through the kings of which town did Aeneas's bloodline lead to Rome's founders?
questions.explanation: Aeneas married a local king's daughter, and his descendants ruled at Alba Longa, a Latin town in the hills south-east of Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: Aeneas married a local king's daughter, and through a long line of kings at Alba Longa, a Latin town in the hills south-east of Rome, his bloodline led to Rome's founders.

questions.question: Men were completely barred from which Roman religious rites?
options: The rites of the Good Goddess
The rites of the Great Mother
questions.explanation: Some of Rome's roughly forty annual festivals belonged to particular groups. The Good Goddess's rites were closed to men entirely.
questions.sourceQuote: Others belonged to particular groups, like the rites of the Good Goddess, from which men were completely barred.
